title: Knowlify vs Icon.me: AI Video Ads or Human-Filmed UGC Compared
summary: Knowlify vs Icon.me: AI ads made for you, or six human-filmed UGC ads for $1,000 with no AI. Compare scope, billing wording, delivery time and rights.
body_markdown:
Choose Knowlify when you want AI video ads made and checked for you, with optional Meta campaign management. Choose Icon when real people must be on camera: its headline offer is six human-filmed, human-edited UGC ads for $1,000. The old Icon.me address redirects to[icon.com](https://icon.com/) , so the current site is icon.com.


Knowlify publishes this guide and sells one of the services compared. We checked Icon's own homepage and pricing page on October 27, 2026, along with Knowlify's public scope. We did not buy Icon's service or test either company's ads.


## Knowlify: our top pick for AI ads made for you


Knowlify is the better fit when speed and volume matter more than a real face. It delivers about 25 finished ads a week, the first batch lands on day 5, and a person checks every ad before delivery. Icon publishes 12 to 16 days for six ads, counted from when the product reaches its creators. The two timelines are not like for like, but they show the gap between filming real people and producing AI video. The three Knowlify formats are AI UGC (AI presenters talking to camera), 3D and stylized character animation, and AI commercials.


You can choose[end-to-end Meta ads](https://knowlify.com/meta-ads-agency) , where Knowlify also runs the campaigns, or creative only if you already have a buyer. Plans start at $5,000 a month. The 90-day guarantee is results-based: if the ads have not made more than you paid in the first 90 days, you can cancel by email for a full refund (terms on the[pricing and guarantee](https://knowlify.com/meta-ads-agency#pricing) page). That 90-day refund applies to creative-only plans; where Knowlify runs the account, the guarantee is an agreed target in 30 days, or you don't pay for the month. When to pick another option: Knowlify does not supply real human creators, so it does not replace Icon when real people must appear on camera.


## What does Icon sell now?


Icon's homepage describes its headline offer as six human UGC ads, filmed and edited by people, for $1,000, labeled "no AI / 100% real" ([Icon](https://icon.com/) ). Icon researches your product and competitors and writes six scripts for you to review before you pay, or you can supply your own. It ships the product to creators, and a Creative Director coaches them as they film. In-house editors cut the footage, and the Creative Director checks every ad. The page lists unlimited human revisions and delivery 12 to 16 days after the product arrives.


The[pricing page](https://icon.com/pricing) lists a $1,000 plan of six human UGC ads, with two creators at three ads each and all concepts unique. A Creative Director takes a live brief within the first 24 hours, and there is a shared Slack channel. Icon says you own the final ads, raw footage and B-roll, with usage rights included, and it offers a 100% money-back guarantee. The page shows Admaker 2.0, Icon's software for tracking progress, reviewing and launching ads and rebooking creators, as part of that plan with no separate price. The site also says Icon originally launched as an AI ad maker, so older write-ups may describe a different product.


## Real creators or AI presenters: which fits your ad?


Icon fits when the proof is a real person's use of the product. Knowlify fits when the ad is a brand statement, a product explanation or an offer, and Knowlify's own rule is that an AI presenter never claims to have used the product. The FTC's testimonial guidance says there is no blanket ban on AI avatars, but an avatar is prohibited when the testimonial it delivers is fake or false ([FTC testimonial Q&A](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/consumer-reviews-testimonials-rule-questions-answers) ).


Creator ads need disclosure as well. When a creator is paid or has another material connection to the brand, the FTC's[influencer guidance](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/disclosures-101-social-media-influencers) explains how that relationship must be shown. Ask Icon how its creators disclose partnerships before you approve scripts.


## How does the cost of an accepted ad compare?


Provider Format Published scope Price as published


Knowlify AI UGC, character animation and AI commercials About 25 finished ads a week; end-to-end Meta or creative only From $5,000 a month


Icon Human-filmed UGC with real creators Six ads from two creators, with unlimited revisions $1,000 for six ads


Brighter Click Fixed batch of creator videos 12 edited videos from four creators, with full usage rights $4,500 for the package


Insense Managed creator UGC Rounds of 8 videos on a 3-month commitment From $3,500 per round


EditClub AI-generated actors, no creators About 60 videos on the Crew plan $1,600 a month for Crew


By our arithmetic, Icon's $1,000 for six ads is about $167 an ad, Brighter Click's $4,500 for 12 edited videos is about $375 each, and EditClub's Crew plan works out to about $27 a video. Knowlify's plans start at $5,000 a month, so ask for a quote that matches the number of accepted ads you need.


Per-file prices are not the whole cost. Count your review time, the revisions you will actually use and any rights you must buy later. Unlimited revisions help only if your approval process can use them.
